objective: V4.3.1 Spark Corpus Migration — convert valuable active memory_items into validated V4 sparks before V4.4 chat wire, so cognitive retrieval has a real living corpus.
context: V4.3 Retrieval + Query is locked and bounded, but the production corpus is still cold-start: roughly 2500 memory_items, 1086 active memory_items, only 3 V4 sparks, and 0 active/pinned sparks at planning time. V4.4 intends to make cognitive memory primary in chat, so the spark corpus must be seeded first. memory_items remain receipts, canon, legacy retrieval, ticket memory, and cold-start fallback; they are not deleted or bulk-archived in this packet.
decisions: Cursor implements all V4.3.1 tickets before V4.4 #363 is claimed.
Migrate value, not rows: do not bulk-convert all memory_items.
Every migrated spark preserves source_memory_item_id and migration lineage.
All generated sparks pass sparks.validate_spark and use sparks.upsert_spark_with_dedup.
Default apply path inserts candidates; only canon/pinned/approved decisions may be promoted active by deterministic policy.
Dry-run reports are required before any apply mode.
memory_items remain intact as receipts and fallback; no deletion, no table removal, no legacy retrieval removal.
No crowley.py rewrite and no CROWLEY_VERSION bump.
risks: Low-signal handoff receipts become noisy sparks
Duplicate canon summaries produce repeated active sparks
Large apply batch is hard to audit or roll back
Migration scripts accidentally mutate production during QA
qa_expectations: Per ticket: focused unit tests for inventory, candidate selection, extraction dry-run, dedup/idempotency, apply batch, lineage, and cognitive context smoke. Full unittest discovery at T5. Any production apply must be small, explicit, and auditable.
next_action: Mint and run this packet before V4.4 #363. Cursor claims T1 first. Do not claim V4.4 until V4.3.1 T5 is approved.

approval.note: Spark corpus migration is required before V4.4 chat wire because V4.3 retrieval is built but the active spark corpus is empty.

tickets.title: V4.3.1 T1: spark corpus inventory and migration policy
tickets.description: Add read-only inventory and policy docs for memory_items → sparks migration. Implement scripts/memory_corpus_inventory.py that reports counts by memory_type/status/source/importance, active memory_items without spark lineage, pinned/canon/high-importance candidates, existing sparks by trust_state/lane, and cold-start retrieval status. Add docs/V4.3.1_SPARK_CORPUS_MIGRATION_PLAN.md documenting selection rules, trust policy, safety guardrails, and apply gates. Files: scripts/memory_corpus_inventory.py, docs/V4.3.1_SPARK_CORPUS_MIGRATION_PLAN.md, tests/test_memory_corpus_inventory.py. Depends on V4.3 lock.
acceptance: Inventory runs read-only and never writes to memory_items or sparks
Report includes total/active memory_items, sparks_total, active/pinned sparks, and active memory_items without source spark lineage
Report breaks down memory_items by memory_type, status, source, importance, pinned
Plan doc defines migrate/include/exclude rules and explicitly says memory_items remain receipts/fallback
Plan doc blocks bulk dumping and requires small explicit apply batches
Tests prove inventory is read-only and schema tolerant

tickets.title: V4.3.1 T2: deterministic candidate selector and dry-run review report
tickets.description: Add scripts/select_memory_spark_candidates.py or equivalent module that selects valuable active memory_items for migration without extracting yet. Prioritize pinned canon summaries, decisions, constraints, lessons, preferences, and high-importance project updates; exclude merged/rejected/staged rows, obvious handoff receipts, QA-only noise, duplicate summaries, side-quest quarantine notes, and rows already represented by sparks.source_memory_item_id. Emit a dry-run JSON/markdown review report with candidate ids, reason, proposed trust tier, and skip reasons. Files: scripts/select_memory_spark_candidates.py, docs/artifacts/ generated only when run, tests/test_memory_spark_candidate_selection.py. Depends on T1.
acceptance: Selector is dry-run/read-only by default
Already-linked memory_items are excluded
Merged/rejected/staged rows are excluded
Pinned canon and durable decisions rank first
Handoff receipt noise and side-quest recovery chatter are skipped unless explicitly high-signal
Report includes include_reason and skip_reason counts
Tests cover include/exclude rules with fixture memory_items

tickets.title: V4.3.1 T3: memory item to spark extraction dry-run
tickets.description: Add scripts/extract_memory_items_to_sparks.py in dry-run mode only. For selected candidates, generate one or more compact validated spark payloads using deterministic mapping for short/canon/decision rows and spark_extraction.extract_sparks_from_text for longer content when allowed. Every proposed spark must pass sparks.validate_spark and include proposed lane, spark_type, certainty, confidence, sensitivity, source_memory_item_id, and lineage_json with migration batch id. No database writes in T3. Files: scripts/extract_memory_items_to_sparks.py, tests/test_memory_to_spark_extraction.py. Depends on T2.
acceptance: Dry-run creates no sparks and does not mutate memory_items
Each proposed spark is atomic and <= 300 chars
Each proposed spark passes sparks.validate_spark
Each proposed spark includes source_memory_item_id and migration lineage
Canon/approved decisions produce confirmed decision/fact sparks when deterministic
Ambiguous long rows stay candidate/proposed with lower confidence or are skipped
Invalid/prompt-injection/secret content is rejected or redacted by existing validation
Tests cover deterministic short-row mapping and long-row dry-run behavior

tickets.title: V4.3.1 T4: small apply batch with idempotent dedup and trust policy
tickets.description: Extend the extraction script with explicit apply mode for small batches only. Apply must require --apply plus --limit and should default to candidate trust_state. Use sparks.upsert_spark_with_dedup and preserve source_memory_item_id/lineage_json. Promote only deterministic canon/pinned/approved decision sparks according to documented policy; otherwise leave candidate. Produce an apply report with inserted/linked/merged/promoted/skipped counts. Files: scripts/extract_memory_items_to_sparks.py, spark_lifecycle.py only if needed, tests/test_memory_to_spark_apply.py. Depends on T3.
acceptance: Apply mode refuses to run without explicit --apply and a bounded --limit
Apply mode is idempotent on repeated runs for same memory_items
All inserted sparks preserve source_memory_item_id
Dedup path links/merges duplicates instead of inserting copies
Default trust_state is candidate
Only documented canon/pinned/approved decision policy can promote active
Apply report includes inserted, linked, merged, promoted, rejected, skipped
Tests prove no bulk apply and no memory_items deletion/archive

tickets.title: V4.3.1 T5: corpus migration lock and cognitive context smoke
tickets.description: Add docs/V4.3.1_SPARK_CORPUS_MIGRATION_LOCK.md recording inventory baseline, candidate policy, dry-run/apply evidence, exact commands, and active spark coverage after the initial small batch. Add smoke tests proving build_cognitive_context can return migrated sparks for core Crowley queries without relying only on memory_items fallback when enough active/pinned sparks exist. Update docs/TICKETS.md to mark V4.3.1 locked and V4.4 unblocked. Run focused suites and full unittest discovery. Depends on T1–T4.
acceptance: Lock doc records before/after counts for memory_items and sparks
Lock doc links dry-run and apply reports
At least core canon/current-project memory is represented as active or pinned sparks, or the lock explicitly records why promotion was held
Cognitive context smoke returns migrated sparks with source_memory_item_id lineage
Cold-start fallback remains available and unchanged
V4.3 retrieval acceptance tests still pass
Actions/crowley_tools registry contract tests still pass
Full unittest discovery passes
docs/TICKETS.md shows V4.3.1 locked and V4.4 next
